scope.graph: Bipartite unweighted n-vertex graphs; bipartition known
scope.space: O(n polylog n) bits for every fixed ε > 0
scope.output: Explicit matching edges, returned after the stream
scope.probability: Deterministic guarantees are available up to 2 − √2 − ε. The 2018 result is randomized with high probability; the lower bound covers randomized constant-error algorithms.
scope.ratioDefinition: r = guaranteed |M| / OPT; larger is better
scope.quantifiers: At most two passes. Every fixed ratio below 2 − √2 is achievable; the plotted endpoint is a limit. Every fixed ratio strictly above 8/9 is excluded. The 2/3 restriction applies only to algorithms retaining solely a greedy matching after pass one.
scope.exclusions: General graphs without a supplied bipartition, random-order streams, three or more passes, weighted matching, value-only estimation, and larger memory budgets are different settings.

coverage: Eight principal algorithm and lower-bound milestones. Equal-limit and weaker historical algorithms remain visible; restricted-class, endpoint-only and RS-dependent results are kept separately. This is a scoped primary-source review, not a claim of exhaustive coverage of every algorithm variant.

results.title: On Graph Problems in a Semi-Streaming Model
results.sourceLocation: Section 3.1, p. 209 of the TCS 2005 journal version
results.statement: Greedy deterministically returns at least half of an optimum matching using one pass and O(n log n) bits; this is also valid with a two-pass budget.
results.notes: Classical baseline documented by this paper. No second pass is needed.

results.authors: Christian Konrad, Frédéric Magniez & Claire Mathieu
results.title: Maximum Matching in Semi-Streaming with Few Passes
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 4 and its proof, pp. 13–14 of arXiv v2 (March 1, 2012); Algorithm 5
results.statement: A deterministic two-pass semi-streaming algorithm returns an explicit matching of size at least (1/2 + 1/52) OPT in bipartite graphs, for every edge order.
results.notes: The theorem displays the rounded improvement 0.019; its proof gives the exact 1/52. The same paper also gives a simpler randomized algorithm with an expected 1/2 + 0.019 guarantee. This row uses the deterministic theorem, so expectation and constant-probability guarantees are not conflated.

results.authors: Hossein Esfandiari, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi & Morteza Monemizadeh
results.title: Finding Large Matchings in Semi-Streaming
results.sourceLocation: Publisher abstract; exact 1/2 + 1/12 and deterministic classification independently checked in Konrad–Naidu 2021, Table 1 and Section 1
results.statement: A deterministic two-pass algorithm obtains a matching of size at least (7/12) OPT in bipartite graphs using O(n) stored edges, hence O(n log n) bits.
results.notes: Pass one finds a maximal matching; pass two stores bounded-degree support edges and then computes a maximum matching in the stored subgraph. The publisher abstract rounds the ratio to 0.583; the exact 7/12 is confirmed by Konrad–Naidu’s primary paper. The original full text was not available in this review.

results.title: Maximum Matching in Two, Three, and a Few More Passes Over Graph Streams
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 5.5 and Algorithm 3; space bound in the introduction
results.statement: A deterministic two-pass algorithm guarantees |M| ≥ (9/16) OPT for triangle-free graphs, hence for bipartite graphs, using O(n log n) bits.
results.notes: Theorem 5.5 gives 1/2 + 1/16 for triangle-free graphs. This is weaker than EHM’s earlier bipartite-only 7/12, but applies to the larger triangle-free class and uses a different greedy augmentation method.

results.title: A Simple Augmentation Method for Matchings with Applications to Streaming Algorithms
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 8 (explicit lower-order term), Theorem 9 and Section 4, pp. 74:8–74:9
results.statement: A randomized two-pass semi-streaming algorithm outputs an explicit bipartite matching with ratio 2 − √2 − o(1), with high probability in n.
results.notes: Theorem 8 has additive loss o(OPT), so 2 − √2 is shown as a limit. Section 4 handles small OPT separately to obtain high probability in n. The algorithm samples first-pass matching edges and uses greedy matchings in two subgraphs during pass two.

results.authors: Sayan Bhattacharya, Peter Kiss, Thatchaphol Saranurak & David Wajc
results.title: Dynamic Matching with Better-than-2 Approximation in Polylogarithmic Update Time
results.sourceLocation: Section 3.1, Observation 3.1, Lemma 3.3, and explicit-matching paragraph after Remark 3.4
results.statement: For every fixed ε > 0, a deterministic two-pass semi-streaming algorithm can output an explicit bipartite matching of size at least (2 − √2 − ε) OPT.
results.notes: The source uses reciprocal approximation 1 + 1/√2 + δ; reparameterizing δ gives the displayed guarantee for any fixed ε. The paper explicitly stores the first-pass matching and second-pass b-matching and computes a maximum matching in their union. Space is Õ(n/δ). Its dynamic size-estimation algorithm is a separate result.

results.shortTitle: Current guarantee also holds on general graphs
results.title: Fully Dynamic Matching: (2 − √2)-Approximation in Polylog Update Time
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 2 and Algorithm 1, Section 4; proof concludes on p. 10
results.statement: For every fixed ε > 0, a deterministic two-pass algorithm outputs matching edges with |M| ≥ (2 − √2 − ε) OPT in general graphs, and therefore in bipartite graphs.
results.notes: This matches the bipartite limit while extending it to general graphs. It stores O(n poly(1/ε)) edges, or O(n poly(1/ε) log n) bits. The endpoint remains a limit; the separate dynamic algorithm in the paper estimates the matching size.

results.title: An Unconditional Lower Bound for Two-Pass Streaming Algorithms for Maximum Matching Approximation
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 6.1 in coauthor Naidu’s thesis, Chapter 6, printed p. 112; proof on pp. 131–133
results.statement: For every fixed ε > 0, any constant-error randomized two-pass algorithm guaranteeing |M| ≥ (8/9 + ε) OPT needs n^{1+Ω(1/(log log n)²)} bits, already on bipartite graphs.
results.notes: This excludes each fixed ratio strictly above 8/9 in semi-streaming space. Equality at 8/9 is not excluded. The hard input is already bipartite; constant error includes success probability at least 2/3.

relatedResults.title: Near-Quadratic Lower Bounds for Two-Pass Graph Streaming Algorithms
relatedResults.statement: Deciding whether an n-vertex bipartite graph has a perfect matching in two passes, with success probability at least 2/3, requires Ω(n² / 2^{Θ(√log n)}) bits.
relatedResults.notes: Consequently exact maximum-matching construction cannot use semi-streaming space. This is an endpoint result, not a fixed subunit approximation ceiling; show only a point at β=1 if included.

relatedResults.shortTitle: A second algorithm at the same limit
relatedResults.title: On Two-Pass Streaming Algorithms for Maximum Bipartite Matching
relatedResults.statement: Combining subsampling with bounded-degree semi-matchings gives a second randomized algorithm approaching 2 − √2, with high probability in OPT.
relatedResults.notes: Its analysis is tight within this parameterized family. That does not prove that 2 − √2 is optimal for all two-pass algorithms.

relatedResults.title: On Two-Pass Streaming Algorithms for Maximum Bipartite Matching
relatedResults.statement: A possibly randomized two-pass algorithm that only retains a greedy maximal matching after its first pass and achieves 2/3 + ε needs n^{1+Ω(1/log log n)} space.
relatedResults.notes: This is a restriction on the entire retained first-pass state. Algorithms retaining other information are not covered; the result must not shade the unrestricted frontier.

relatedResults.title: A Two-Pass Lower Bound for Semi-Streaming Maximum Matching
relatedResults.statement: A two-pass semi-streaming algorithm with success probability at least 2/3 is constrained by the density of Ruzsa–Szemerédi graphs. Known constructions give a near-one, n-dependent barrier; stronger RS-density assumptions give a constant barrier.
relatedResults.notes: The paper gives 0.98 as an illustrative excluded ratio under RS(n)=n^{1−o(1)}. It is not an unconditional 0.98 threshold. The 2024 unconditional 8/9 ceiling is stronger even than this hypothetical case; retain this as history, not a current numerical frontier.

searchSummary: Primary-source checks and targeted 2025/2026 searches through 2026-10-20 located no better same-scope constant algorithmic limit or stronger unconditional constant lower-bound ceiling. Publication status is distinguished from evidence access; EHM2016 is checked through its publisher abstract and KN2021’s explicit primary-paper cross-reference.
